business_scope.primary_industry_name: Single-Origin Green Arabica Coffee Bean Container Distribution

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention) - in force for Luxembourg
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties applicable to Luxembourg, including the BLEU-Colombia Investment Protection Agreement (in force since 12 November 2014)

EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA, in force 1 August 2020) and EU-Vietnam Investment Protection Agreement (signed 30 June 2019, ratification pending) - trade and investment framework for green coffee imports from Vietnam

Luxembourg double taxation treaty (DTA) network with principal coffee-origin and transit states, including the Luxembourg-Colombia, Luxembourg-Brazil, and Luxembourg-Vietnam DTAAs applicable to trading margins, royalties, and financial flows
Convention on the Settlement of Investment Disputes between States and Nationals of Other States (ICSID Convention) - Luxembourg is a Contracting State

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Companies Act 1915, including the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 27 July 2023 implementing the CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022 (Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT professional obligations, as amended.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access suspended since 22 November 2022; only competent authorities, notaries, bailiffs, and professional obliged entities have registered access; data is disclosed to law enforcement and tax authorities without partner consent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate corporate general partner or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the country of origin (domestic commercial register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / legal existence certificate of the corporate partner
UBO attestation or register extract evidencing the ultimate beneficial owners of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domestic UBO registry or certified company secretary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Luxembourg formation agent and notary to incorporate the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the signing partner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of the general partner, limited partners, and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular officer in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each contributing limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or certified public accountant in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, UBOs, and material counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN/446 List (for USD Swift wire and documentary letter-of-credit corridors), the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance domestic sanctions lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction monitoring. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and their family members and close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence per Articles 3-3, 3-4, and 5 of the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Continuous monitoring is required, with re-screening upon any change in partners, admission of a new limited partner, or material change in the ownership chain.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal at www.lbr.lu, operating the Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) and the Recueil electronique des societes (RESA); filings are also processed via the MyGuichet.lu e-administration gateway.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All RCS filings and the SCSp partnership agreement must be in French, German, or Luxembourgish, or accompanied by a certified translation into one of these languages. The fixed corporate denomination must be written in Latin characters; non-Latin scripts are not accepted. The name must include the suffix 'SCSp' or the full designation 'Societe en commandite speciale'. The denomination must be distinctive, lawful, not misleading, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already registered in the RCS or to protected national or EU trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Banking (reserved to CSSF-licensed credit institutions)
Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Reassurance (reserved to CAA-licensed undertakings)
Investment Fund, Fonds, SICAV, SICAF, OPC, UCITS, AIF (reserved to CSSF-authorized collective investment schemes or managers)
Stock Exchange, Bourse (requires Ministry of Finance approval)
Trust, Fiduciary, Fiduciaire (regulated fiduciary activity under the Law of 10 August 1991)
Audit, Reviseur d'entreprises (reserved to members of IRE/ISCA)
Notary, Notaire, Lawyer, Avocat, Bailiff, Huissier (reserved liberal professions)
Chamber of Commerce, Chambre de Commerce
University, Universite, School, Ecole (requires Ministry of Education authorization)
Luxembourg, Letzebuerg, or Grand-Ducal as leading or dominant tokens (deemed emblematic and misleading without administrative tolerance)
Sovereign and state-emblematic terms: Royal, Imperial, National, Ministere, Gouvernement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 101-1 to 101-17 as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the statement of solvency; Law of 16 May 2018 on the electronic publication of central legal acts (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société / acte constitutif) together with the RCS filing form (formulaire B) and beneficial ownership declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement applies to an SCSp; partners freely determine capital contributions in the partnership agreement; no paid-up capital or escrow account is mandated by Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned general partner, acting as the managing organ of the Société en Commandite Spéciale, hereby resolves: (1) the capital subscriptions tendered by the limited partners under the partnership agreement are accepted in full, with the initial contribution for specialty green coffee bean trading fixed at EUR 50,000 (or as stated); (2) the registered office is adopted at the address stated in the partnership agreement, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) the sole general partner appoints [Name] as gérant with day-to-day management power and separate signatory capacity for banking and customs operations; (4) the gérant is authorized to execute all filings before the Trade and Companies Register and to procure the applicable food business and warehouse registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal, www.lbr.lu / RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary search in the RCS business name database to confirm that the proposed SCSp name is distinct, lawful and does not contravene Luxembourg public order. Submit an online name reservation request through the LBR portal or instruct counsel to obtain a negative certificate from the RCS. The name must be followed by 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'.
required_dossiers: Name reservation form
Identity document of the general partner
Power of attorney if filed by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of identity or confusion with an existing registration, file a fresh reservation with a modified, clearly distinguishable name; no formal appeal is needed, but legal counsel may contest an arbitrary refusal through a writ before the District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and legal counsel; subsequent filing with RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement (acte constitutif) containing the exact SCSp name, the address of the registered office, the capital contributions and share of profits of the general and limited partners, the scope of business (import and wholesale distribution of specialty green coffee beans under ISIC 4631), the rules for management, the identity of the gérant, and whether legal personality has been excluded. Execute the agreement by private deed, unless the partners opt for legal personality, in which case the deed must be notarized before a Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Full text of the partnership agreement
Statement of the contributions of each partner
List of partners with beneficial ownership details
Copies of identity documents of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If LBR or the notary identifies missing or inconsistent clauses, correct the agreement via an amending deed or private affidavit; re-execute the relevant pages and refile with an explanatory cover letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via online e-file or counter at the Luxembourg District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the signed partnership agreement and complete the RCS standard form (formulaire B) identifying the general partner, limited partners, registered office, duration, and legal form. Submit the filing through the LBR e-Filing portal or directly to the RCS registry of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg. Attach the certificate of domiciliation of the registered office, the beneficial ownership declaration (RCB form), and proof of identity of the natural-person general partner or the general partner's own registration extract if a legal entity. Pay the registration and publication fees.
required_dossiers: Signed original/certified copy of the partnership agreement
RCS filing form (formulaire B)
Certificate of the registered office address (bail or occupancy consent)
Identity document and residence proof of the general partner
RCB beneficial ownership declaration
For a corporate general partner: excerpt from its own trade register and board resolution approving its role
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or gap list, submit a remedial filing within the given deadline (usually 15 days) correcting the defective annex; for substantive refusals, appeal before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 40 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS accepts the registration, the registrar shall generate the legal publication extract and transmit it to RESA. Monitor the RESA portal to verify that the SCSp's constitution, identity of the general partner and registered office have been duly published. The publication serves both publicity and, where the SCSp has opted for legal personality, the activation of the entity's legal capacity and the limitation of liability of limited partners.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RESA publication order/receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or contains an error, request an immediate correction from the competent LBR registrar; if publication is refused, apply to the District Court with jurisdiction over commercial registries for a rectification order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, National Business and Social Security Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – VAT department; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration application (form 300) via the ACD online portal (MyGuichet) to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number, using the RCS certificate and the business purpose as proof of economic activity. Register with the CCSS if the SCSp will hire employees or appoint a managing director subject to the social security framework; otherwise submit a nil employer declaration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Detailed activity description (ISIC 4631 – wholesale of green coffee beans)
General partner identification
Taxpayer identification number request
LEI application if required for banking and customs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or CCSS questions the application, correct and resubmit the digital form through MyGuichet; in the event of an unfavourable VAT ruling, file a challenge with the Director of the ACD within 40 days and, if necessary, to the Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Operator Registration for Import and Wholesale of Specialty Green Coffee Beans
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de la Sécurité Alimentaire (ASA), Ministry of Health, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because coffee beans are foodstuffs for human consumption, the SCSp must be registered as a food business operator prior to placing products on the Luxembourg market. Submit the online registration via the ASA portal or MyGuichet, indicating the import, storage and wholesale distribution of green coffee beans. Provide operational details of the warehouse, the import volumes, the traceability system and the hazard analysis summary for handling dry agricultural commodities.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate
VAT number
Food business operator registration form
Description of storage site and handling process
Traceability and recall procedures
Proof of compliance with EC No 178/2002 and EC No 852/2004 hygiene requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ASA issues a non-conformity, respond within 10 working days with a corrective action plan and updated procedures; if registration is refused, request an administrative review before the Minister of Health, then appeal to the Administrative Tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Commerce; administrative food safety authority: Administration de la Sécurité Alimentaire (ASA); environmental authority: Administration de l'Environnement (AEV)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement) and Food Business Operator Registration (Green Coffee Bean Import and Wholesale Distribution)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement / Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Développement durable (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Registration / simple declaration regime under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment (no full EIA report required for dry storage of green coffee beans under 50,000 tonnes storage capacity; subject to standard administrative clearance)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge from coffee bean processing; all site stormwater run-off must meet the national threshold for suspended solids and hydrocarbons before discharge (LuxEMV standards; limit values for phenols and VOCs do not apply absent roasting or industrial extraction); dust management and solid organic waste handling must follow the national waste management plan and EU Waste Framework Directive; no chlorofluorocarbon or ozone-depleting emissions; use ECOGARAGES or closed bin storage to mitigate entrainment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) issued on the basis of a site inspection of the warehouse, confirming exit routes, extinguishing systems and compliance with the Luxembourg fire regulations; structural load inspection certificate for the commercial warehouse proving suitability for stacked green coffee pallet loads; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), covering employee exposure to organic dust, safe handling of jute and burlap bags, forklift traffic management, and the establishment of a risk assessment under the Law of 17 June 1994 on workplace safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) - Registration Duties and VAT Administration; official e-portal: MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.public.lu; direct income tax administration: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp must first be registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) to obtain its national business registration number (matricule). For VAT, a non-established taxable person applies to the AED before making taxable supplies: EU-established operators file the standard VAT registration application directly, accompanied by articles of incorporation, board power of attorney and proof of economic activity; operators established outside the EEA appoint and disclose an AED-approved fiscal representative who files in the representative's name. The AED issues a separate Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by eight digits. Because the SCSp is income-tax transparent, no ACD corporate tax registration is required at entity level; partners report their shares in their respective home-country tax registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate and personal income tax (look-through), so profits and losses are allocated to partners; for VAT the SCSp is nevertheless a taxable person in its own right and holds its own Luxembourg VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime; partnership transparency is the statutory default. Under the amended Article 175 LIR, an SCSp carrying on a commercial activity and having exclusively corporate joint and several or limited partners is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax at entity level; in other circumstances the default look-through treatment applies and no elective entity-level tax election is available. Advance tax rulings may be obtained from the ACD for prospective transactions, and the ATAD hybrid and reverse-hybrid rules (Law of 21 December 2017, as amended) override any mismatches arising from partner-country classification. No separate US-style hybrid election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), harmonised under EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small businesses as the VAT franchise threshold; no de minimis turnover exemption applies to non-established foreign entities, which must register with the AED as soon as they intend to make taxable supplies in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose a general B2B real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping or continuous transaction control reporting. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory through the PEPPOL infrastructure for public-supply invoices; B2B and B2C invoices may be issued electronically under the invoicing rules of the Luxembourg VAT Code and the VAT Directive, subject to the authenticity, integrity and readability requirements, without prior AED clearance or pre-clearance fiscal stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of green arabica coffee beans (HS 0901) exported by the SCSp to customers outside the EU qualify for the 0% rate under Article 146(1)(a) of the VAT Directive, provided the seller holds documentary proof that the goods left the EU within the statutory period (generally 90 days from dispatch) and that delivery occurred to the non-EU customer. Intra-EU container distribution to a customer holding a valid Luxembourg and destination-state VAT registration number is an exempt intra-Community supply at 0% if the VIES recapitulative statement and the customer's VAT validation confirm the B2B trade. The 0% export rate applies only upon complete export evidence; otherwise the supply is reportable under Luxembourg domestic categories, which include the 3% super-reduced rate for foodstuffs or the 17% standard rate, and must be self-assessed accordingly.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (SAD) - EU customs export declaration discharged by the Luxembourg or point-of-departure customs office
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical departure of the container from EU territory
Commercial invoice identifying the SCSp as supplier and describing single-origin green arabica coffee beans under HS 0901
Packing list and container manifest matching the SAD quantities
Swift MT103 or documentary letter of credit settlement documentation together with an Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing foreign-exchange remittance within the contractual term
VAT registration validation output and VIES listing where intra-EU distribution is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AED and customs auditors may reopen export zero-rating claims for five years, extended to ten years where elements of fraud or evasion are proven. Missing, inconsistent or fraudulent export proof causes recharacterisation of the turnover as a Luxembourg or intra-Community taxable supply at 17%, with default interest computed on a monthly basis and administrative fines of up to the tax evaded. Material false declarations may attract criminal penalties, including fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment, and the general partners of the SCSp may be held jointly and severally liable for the clawed-back VAT, interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Luxembourg's central bank and member of the Eurosystem. Prudential and anti-money laundering supervision of credit institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the BCL operates TARGET2 settlement and collects Balance of Payments and International Investment Position statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone jurisdiction with full and unrestricted convertibility of the euro under Article 63 TFEU; capital and current account operations are liberalised both within the EU/EEA and toward third countries. No exchange controls, no prior authorisation for cross-border payments, and no remittance impediment on profits distributed by a fiscally transparent SCSp (pass-through). Payment instructions must nevertheless be tagged with the correct Balance of Payments reporting code, and the resident bank must complete AML/KYC verification prior to any execution. For green coffee import transactions from non-EEA origins (e.g., Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia), funds may be freely paid and received in EUR or USD without central bank approval; the only statutory constraints are EU asset-freezing and sanctions measures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law and BCL regulations impose no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline. Export receivables in USD or EUR may be held freely in foreign-currency accounts. The only statutory duty is the balance-of-payments and direct-investment reporting obligation under ECB Regulation (EU) No 184/2014, implemented by BCL circulars; the resident commercial bank files transaction-level reports with the BCL, and each cross-border operation must be assigned the correct classification code (category S — direct investment / trade in goods).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Trade Finance Account
Operational Account with Documentary LC Desk
Operational Account and Trade Finance Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium feasibility. Luxembourg recognises CSSF-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and PSD2 passporting of EEA EMIs. For a specialty green coffee SCSp, a digital EMI may handle only ancillary operational payments (sub-threshold supplier prepayments, payroll, utilities) and cannot support documentary letters of credit, trade finance, or large-scale USD clearing. Offshore or non-EEA EMIs are not viable: they cannot lawfully hold in-scope euro payment accounts for a Luxembourg partnership, cannot execute SWIFT MT103 payments to coffee exporters at commercial scale, and would create an unrecognised money-transmission nexus for tax, AML and balance-of-payments reporting. The SCSp should designate a Tier-1 commercial bank as the primary liquidity rail and use EMIs solely as a secondary, low-value operating channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandated for the general partner (associé commandité) or at least one authorised signatory of the SCSp at the account-opening meeting in Luxembourg. Most Tier-1 banks require an in-person KYC interview before activating payment rails, with fully remote onboarding for non-resident partnerships generally rejected. Some banks (notably BGL BNP Paribas and BCEE) permit a hybrid process: video identification of the UBOs followed by an in-person signature session at the bank's Luxembourg headquarters or before a Luxembourg notary or regulated corporate-services provider. Remote opening is realistic only where the general partner is itself a supervised Luxembourg entity. At the interview, the bank verifies identity documents, corporate powers, the capital-call resolution, and the complete organisational chart of the SCSp; a mere power of attorney will not be accepted for signatories who have never been met by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity: three or more tiers of partnership or LLC ownership obscuring the natural-person controllers of the SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register per CSSF Regulation 12-02 listing all natural persons holding a direct or indirect interest above 25%; signed organisational chart approved by the general partner; certified passports and proof of address for each UBO; Luxembourg criminal record certificate (casier judiciaire) of the general partner; and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat affirming the SCSp structure and the clear identification of the associé commandité.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds verification on capital injections originating from offshore holding companies or commodity-trade capital pools.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements for each contributing partner; audited financial statements or an auditor's comfort letter; evidence of profitable commodity trades comprising sales invoices and purchase contracts; signed source-of-wealth declaration (déclaration d'origine des fonds et du patrimoine); and tax-residence certificates of all contributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax classification confusion: the bank may suspect that the SCSp is a taxable corporate vehicle or an unregulated collective investment scheme.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership deed; RCS Luxembourg registration extract confirming the SCSp legal form; Luxembourg tax-counsel opinion confirming transparent tax treatment under the law of 23 July 2016; confirmation that the SCSp will not carry on regulated activities requiring a CSSF licence; and a written treasury mandate confining activities to physical commodity trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP and adverse-country-risk flags generated by coffee-origin counterparties in Ethiopia, Brazil, Colombia, Indonesia or other non-EEA states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results from the bank's sanctions and PEP systems (e.g., Fircosoft or Oracle screening reports); ICC certificates of origin; phytosanitary certificates; transport documents including container-level bills of lading; complete supplier registration packs for each exporter; standard EU and UN sanctions clauses in purchase contracts; and beneficial-ownership evidence of the foreign supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering suspicion: potential over- or under-invoicing on bulk green coffee container transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented pricing basis against the relevant reference benchmark (ICE Futures US Arabica C-contract or ICO composite indicator); independent pre-shipment inspection certificates from SGS or Bureau Veritas; proof that invoiced unit prices fall within the bank's accepted 5–15% commodity-price validation band; and a complete transactional trail from purchase order, proforma invoice, LC or MT103, bill of lading, customs Single Administrative Document (SAD) and final warehouse receipt.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial and subsequent capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 wire transfer (or SEPA/TARGET2 for euro) into the SCSp's dedicated Capital Escrow Account at a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. The payment message must reference the capital-call article of the SCSp partnership agreement, the capital-call notice number, and the Balance of Payments purpose code S301 (acquisition of share capital, direct-investment category) under the ECB Vademecum. Before the first inbound transfer, the bank must hold: (i) an RCS extract evidencing registration of the SCSp; (ii) the executed partnership agreement; (iii) the capital-call resolution adopted by the general partner; and (iv) the complete KYC/UBO pack of the remitting investor. For wires above EUR 1,000,000, the bank will normally trigger enhanced due diligence and expects pre-advice up to 48 hours before value date. Upon credit, funds remain frozen in the escrow account until compliance releases them to the operational account against a written activation request.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Green coffee container purchases are settled through two principal clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account and prepayment terms with repeat, vetted suppliers, typically 30–60% prepayment with the balance settled against presentation of shipping documents; and (b) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700, payable at sight or by deferred payment at 60–120 days, in favour of the foreign exporter, primarily for first-time origin suppliers. Euro payments clear across TARGET2 through the BCL; US-dollar payments are routed through the bank's New York correspondent (e.g., JPMorgan Chase, Citibank or BNP Paribas New York) over CHIPS or Fedwire. Disbursements must match the invoice, proforma invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, and the bank's trade-finance price-verification rules. Any discrepancy in the documentary presentation must be cured by a discrepancy waiver or an LC amendment via MT707 before release of goods. For amounts exceeding the bank's single-transaction threshold (typically EUR 250,000–500,000), the treasury must submit a trade-settlement instruction with the underlying contract summary at least one business day in advance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (plain vanilla) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex against a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank dealing room; the SCSp, acting as a non-financial counterparty (NFC-), is exempt from the EMIR clearing obligation provided the OTC derivative clearing threshold is not breached, while all trades remain subject to EMIR reporting to an authorised trade repository.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EUR/BRL, EUR/COP, EUR/ETB and EUR/IDR for hedging green coffee purchase-price exposure against emerging-market supplier currencies, net-settled in EUR or USD against an agreed fixing source.
FX swaps converting surplus USD export receivables into EUR for treasury liquidity management, executed under the resident bank's Standard Settlement Instructions (SSIs).
Cross-currency swaps aligning USD trade-loan liabilities with the EUR functional currency of the SCSp where foreign-exchange-funded trade facilities are used.

Plain-vanilla EUR/USD FX options (European-style puts and calls) as premium-based hedges where the SCSp treasury policy permits option hedging; execution is subject to CSSF suitability rules and MiFID II client-classification confirmation before trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data confirmation (confirmation annuelle au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for calendar-year entities; entities with different financial year-ends must file on the anniversary-date cycle specified by the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SCSp to administrative fines under the amended RCS Law of 19 December 2002; continued non-compliance after formal notice may lead to administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation (confirmation annuelle au Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual UBO confirmation is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to EUR 250,000 and, for natural persons, imprisonment; persistent non-compliance can suspend partner rights and expose the manager (gérant) to personal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) where mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year close; for a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit is subject to administrative penalty and coercive daily fines imposed by the RCS; repeated failure to file may result in court-ordered strike-off and loss of legal personality

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé is required if the SCSp or its Luxembourg group exceeds two of the three statutory thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees; audit is also mandatory for regulated entities such as banks, insurance undertakings, and certain investment funds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the annual accounts of commercial companies; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is permitted for voluntarily consolidated or listed-group purposes

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an up-to-date UBO register and submit an annual confirmation to the RBE by 31 March; transfers of partnership interests or changes in profit-sharing ratios are effective contractually and must be reflected in the RBE within one month, while the annual confirmation attests the accuracy of the standing data as at the filing date; the gérant or a Luxembourg approved professional must file in electronic form and require no notarial re-authentication unless a notarised deed is otherwise required under the partnership agreement
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers (gérants) and General Partner Decisions
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions and Management Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 3,500 per annum for a Luxembourg registered office/domiciliation service and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – 8,500 for a small to mid-size SCSp where a statutory audit is triggered; no mandatory audit cost arises below the statutory thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate standard Luxembourg City rate applicable to a fully taxable corporate taxpayer (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT base + 6.75% municipal business tax). The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default and is not itself subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax on its allocated income; the economic tax burden is imposed on the partners in their residence jurisdictions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Default pass-through classification of the SCSp; no Luxembourg income tax at entity level on green coffee trading profits; participation exemption available to qualifying corporate partners for dividends and capital gains; no Luxembourg withholding tax on distributions from a transparent SCSp; exclusion from the minimum net wealth tax where the SCSp holds no taxable Luxembourg PE assets; ATAD-aligned interest limitation and anti-hybrid rules remain applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual partnership tax declaration of the SCSp (transparent entity schedule) filed with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via the Luxembourg electronic filing portal (MyGuichet.lu / eDeclaration). Corporate partners receiving the allocated income additionally file their own Luxembourg corporate income tax return (Form 600 CIT/NWT package) where they are Luxembourg residents or maintain a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The SCSp declaration and the partner returns are due no later than 31 December of the year following the accounting year; electronic filing with a certified tax advisor normally extends the administrative deadline to 31 March of the second year following the accounting year. A written extension may be obtained from the ACD before the statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp registered name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, LEI code, registered office address, and identification of the general partner and its managers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg registered office. Non-resident partners are not listed in Box 1; they are identified in the partner allocation schedule only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the entity is a Société en Commandite Spéciale governed by the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended and that it has not elected taxable (non-transparent) status for Luxembourg income tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the default transparent classification. A non-resident partner cannot independently alter the entity's classification; any elective taxation must be filed by the general partner before the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Accounting Year, Currency, and Valuation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period, closing date, accounting currency, and FX conversion method. Green coffee import transactions denominated in USD require booking at the ECB reference rate on the transaction date; inventory valuation of containerized green coffee beans must follow accepted commercial methods (weighted average or FIFO).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep full container-level documentation: bills of lading, certificates of origin, phytosanitary certificates, and commodity purchase agreements. The ACD may require these where cross-border related party purchases of specialty green coffee are examined.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Net Result Allocated to Partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit or loss of the SCSp for the fiscal year after deducting all directly attributable expenses: green coffee cost of goods sold, ocean freight, marine insurance, silo storage fees, warehouse costs, brokerage commissions, and interest on working capital financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable profit is allocated pro rata to partners under the partnership agreement. Non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg tax on this allocation unless the SCSp is treated as having a Luxembourg permanent establishment; no Luxembourg withholding tax is applied on the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of controlled transactions with associated enterprises: purchases of green coffee from the origin-country affiliate, management fees, guarantee fees, intercompany loans, and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner controls the origin supplier, the transaction must satisfy the arm's length principle using a CUP method benchmarked against international green coffee price indices (e.g., ICO composite price or exchange-applicable differential-plus-freight benchmarks). Maintain a contemporaneous pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Municipal Business Tax and Net Wealth Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of whether the SCSp conducts activity through a Luxembourg fixed place of business such that municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) or net wealth tax schedules are triggered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure holding, financing, or distribution SCSp with no Luxembourg office, staff, or recurring decision-making will normally not be subject to municipal business tax or net wealth tax. Any substance in Luxembourg, including silo or warehousing arrangements in Luxembourg, must be consistently disclosed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of up to EUR 1,250 per declaration; overdue assessed taxes bear late-payment interest of 0.6% per commenced month (7.2% p.a.); incomplete or intentionally false declarations expose the general partner and the SCSp to reassessment, fines up to EUR 250,000, publication of the conviction, and criminal imprisonment of up to five years for tax fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on allocations and distributions made by the transparent SCSp to its partners. A transparent SCSp is not a Luxembourg withholding tax payor, and its distributions are not legally classified as dividends. By contrast, if the green coffee trading activity were instead held through a fully taxable Luxembourg S.à r.l. or SA, the statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax rate is 15%, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and to 0%-5% under most Luxembourg double tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For SCSp pass-through flows, no Luxembourg withholding tax arises and therefore no treaty relief form is required at the entity level. For any Luxembourg-resident corporate payor distributing dividends to a non-resident partner, the reduced or zero treaty rate is applied at source only after: (i) receipt by the paying entity of an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the partner's residence; (ii) submission of an ownership declaration evidencing the qualifying shareholding and, where applicable, the 12-month holding period; and (iii) for EU cases, confirmation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption or a refund application to the ACD where tax was withheld in excess. The refund path in Luxembourg requires the standard ACD treaty relief form, the original TRC, the dividend resolution, and proof of actual payment and withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Luxembourg imposes no general withholding tax on outbound royalties paid to non-residents; the statutory rate is 0%, so DTA royalty articles are largely irrelevant to a green coffee importing structure (noting that brand, marketing, or processing IP held offshore must still satisfy substance conditions). Interest: Luxembourg imposes no general withholding tax on bank or commercial interest paid to non-resident lenders; the statutory rate is 0%. The ATAD interest limitation rule, which cap net deductible interest at 30% of EBITDA (EUR 3 million threshold), and the EU anti-hybrid rules remain enforceable regardless of the 0% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory where the consolidating multinational group exceeds EUR 750,000,000 in annual consolidated revenue. Luxembourg has no published statutory minimum threshold for the Local File and Master File; in administrative practice the ACD requests the OECD transfer pricing documentation package where related-party flows engaged by the SCSp exceed approximately EUR 1,000,000 per annum, and a contemporaneous Local File must always be prepared where commodity pricing deviates from published green coffee benchmarks.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not impose a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime, but the statutory General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 6 of the General Tax Law), the ATAD abuse clause, and ACD administrative doctrine require genuine substance: local registered office, Luxembourg-based management decisions, active commercial negotiation of coffee supply contracts, bank accounts, books and records in Luxembourg, and physical presence commensurate with the activity. An SCSp that executes all green coffee procurement, logistics, insurance, and financing decisions from the origin country will be re-characterized as managed from abroad, exposing the structure to a Luxembourg permanent establishment assessment, denial of treaty benefits under the OECD Principal Purpose Test, or annulment of the partnership's Luxembourg tax transparency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Artificial Inventory Loss Construction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately misstating the cost of imported single-origin green coffee, fabricating container or warehouse destruction records, underreporting coffee volumes, or creating artificial losses through inflated intercompany purchase prices from the origin affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of hidden profits; administrative fine up to EUR 250,000; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal tax fraud prosecution with imprisonment of up to five years and publication of the guilty verdict.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and its directors may be jointly and severally liable for the SCSp's unpaid taxes; in fraud cases courts may pierce the partnership shield, attach personal assets of the directors, issue travel bans, and impose personal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp with no Luxembourg office, employees, bank accounts, or decision-making while routing coffee distribution profits through Luxembourg solely to benefit from fiscal transparency and treaty protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR requalification of the structure; retroactive withdrawal of tax transparency; denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; adjustment of taxable basis to the true economic beneficiary; fines and publication of the reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Direct disqualification from managing Luxembourg entities, joint and several liability for the reassessed taxes and penalties, and criminal prosecution for aiding an abusive tax arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within one month of incorporation or any ownership change, or knowingly concealing the identity of the true origin-country coffee counterparty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 under the Luxembourg AML framework (Law of 12 November 2004 and RBE Law of 13 January 2019); criminal sanctions with imprisonment of up to five years; freezing of distributions and closure of banking facilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability of the general partner's directors; travel bans and extradition exposure where the concealment forms part of a cross-border money-laundering operation; civil damages to creditors and co-investors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing a false SCSp declaration: declaring the partnership dormant while container movements continue, omitting silo inventory profits, using unbenchmarked transfer prices with the affiliated green coffee exporter, or falsely denying a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Correction of the taxable basis, fines up to EUR 250,000, publication of the conviction, and imprisonment of eight days to five years under Luxembourg tax criminal law applicable to directors and tax representatives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the SCSp limited liability on proof of bad faith: personal recovery of the entire tax debt, disqualification from corporate management, freeze of personal bank accounts, and potential extradition if the director is resident abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing specialty green coffee from sanctioned jurisdictions or transport companies, laundering the origin through false bills of lading, or handling payments through jurisdictions under EU/UN/OFAC embargo while using the Luxembourg SCSp as a payment intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Freezing of assets and funds by the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; customs and excise penalties up to the full value of the goods plus fines up to EUR 250,000; criminal sanctions under Luxembourg and EU sanctions regulations, including imprisonment of up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Direct personal liability of the general partner's directors for sanctions violations; travel bans, asset freezes, and confiscation of personal property; criminal prosecution simultaneously in Luxembourg and the originating jurisdiction.
